name: DPD Thermostat
description: Dissipative particle dynamics in 2D: soft repulsion, a pair drag −gamma·(1 − x)²·v_dot and a pair noise sigma·(1 − x)·randn, all along the line of centers, plus a weak spring between every pair (½·k·r², a trap that follows the drop's own center of mass). The square starts frozen at T = 0; the noise melts it into a round drop, the temperature overshoots while it relaxes, then settles where drag balances noise, near T = sigma²·dt/(2·gamma) = 1 (Statistics). Every random kick is equal and opposite on its pair, so the noise adds no net momentum (the implicit drag step keeps it only approximately: the drop drifts very slowly). Try: disable Pair noise and it freezes; disable Pair drag and it heats without bound; double sigma for T = 4.
